$comment: Lighthouse CI config for nocturne (slot 8, PLAN Phase 7) — DESKTOP profile.
Audits the BUILT + SERVED production surface on :3100 (next build --webpack
&& next start, NEVER next dev — the strict ADR-002 §6 CSP forbids unsafe-eval
and next dev cannot run under it; the meld/atrium/apex lesson).
TARGET = /about, NOT /. This is the apex precedent applied to a generative
piece. The / route is a CONTINUOUSLY-ANIMATING, audio-reactive WebGL canvas
(frameloop='always' while armed — ADR-002 §5). Two facts make / an unfair,
confounded Lighthouse-performance subject, and BOTH are by design:
1. Headless Lighthouse runs on software-GL (SwiftShader): a 262k additive
field + bloom takes multi-second frames there (an artefact of no GPU,
not the app). On a real GPU the field holds 60fps (the zero-per-particle-
CPU-work invariant, ADR-002 §1) — but a headless TBT/CPU measurement of
the live canvas measures SwiftShader, not the product.
2. A continuous render loop intrinsically spends main-thread time every
frame; an audio-reactive field cannot be 'demand'-driven like apex's
idle configurator (the deliberate apex divergence, ADR-002 §5).
The canvas route's 60fps + the four perf tiers are therefore measured and
documented SEPARATELY (the engine verifier + the real-GPU deploy GIF), NOT
Lighthouse-asserted — exactly the honest stance apex took for its canvas
section and tape took for its live route. /about is the clean, static,
server-rendered NON-canvas surface (no WebGL, no audio, no canvas at all):
the right Lighthouse subject, and it is the SEO + screen-reader view of the
piece anyway.
Asserts CLAUDE.md § 4 / PLAN success criteria on /about: >= 95 in ALL FOUR
categories, median of 5 runs, plus the Core Web Vitals / first-paint targets
(LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, FCP < 1.8s, TBT proxy for INP < 200ms).
LHCI starts the server itself via startServerCommand.
